findings.title: removeOne() with a negative index removes the wrong element and corrupts the queue
findings.property: removeOne(i) behaves like Array.prototype.splice(i,1) on the equivalent array, including negative indices, leaving the remaining items intact
findings.actual: returns 2 but the queue becomes [undefined, 1]-like corrupted state (the front slot is cleared and head advanced instead of removing the last item)
findings.evidence: removeOne explicitly accepts negative indices (range check i < -size, then i += size), and peekAt documents negative indices as counting from the end. The shifting branch is chosen with the un-normalised `index` (index < size/2), so a negative index always takes the front branch with a zero-iteration loop.

error.message:
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual - expected

  [
+   undefined
-   1
  ]

review.title: removeOne() with a negative index corrupts the queue because the branch choice uses the un-normalised index
review.reason: removeOne explicitly accepts negative indices (`i < -size` is rejected, otherwise `i += size`), but the branch test `index < size / 2` and the loop counters still use the original `index`. With index -1, the front branch is taken with a zero-iteration loop. It then clears the slot of the last element and advances `_head`, so the queue ends up as [undefined] instead of [1]. The fix is to use the normalised `i` for the branch test and loop counts, which a maintainer would accept.

findings.title: remove() with a negative index and count > 1 removes the wrong items and corrupts the queue
findings.property: remove(i, n) behaves like Array.prototype.splice(i, n), including negative i
findings.actual: queue is left with undefined holes and wrong contents
findings.evidence: remove() accepts negative indices (i < -size check, i += size) but the later branches use the raw `index` (index + count === size, index === 0, index < 0) instead of the normalised i.

review.title: remove() with a negative index and count > 1 corrupts the queue
review.reason: remove() explicitly accepts negative indices (`i < -size` check, then `i += size`). After that, the multi-item branches still test and use the raw `index` (`index + count === size`, `index === 0`, `this._head + index + count`, `index < 0`) instead of the normalised `i`. For `remove(-3, 2)` on [1,2,3,4], none of the fast paths match and the middle-removal branch uses a negative `index`. That leaves `undefined` holes and wrong contents, as the repro shows. The `count === 1` path uses the normalised `i` and works, and positive indices are unaffected, so this is an incomplete normalisation that a maintainer would fix.
